title.narrative: Multi-sectoral support in China camp and Woinshet site, Debre Birhan city of Amhara region for internally displaced people

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis multi-sector emergency response initiative will be implemented by Norwegian Church Aid (NCA), in partnership with the Ethiopian Orthodox Church Development and Inter-Church Aid Commission (EOC-DICAC), and the Amhara Women's Association (AWA), a women-led organisation, in the North Shewa Zone of the Amhara Region. The 9-month project aims to deliver integrated assistance to 20,185 vulnerable IDPs in collective centres informal settlements in China Woinshet camps in Debre Berhan town. The response will combine interventions in the areas of camp CCCM, ES/NFI, WASH, health and nutrition, protection (including GBV and general protection). Cash assistance will be the default modality to ensure flexible and dignified assistance, while in-kind support will be provided where market conditions require it. With 80% of women in its SMT, NCA will focus on building the capacity of partners, providing technical support ensuring project compliance. It will also provide close monitoring follow-up of project implementation to ensure the project's effectiveness efficiency. The NCA will also implement activities directly in the health, nutrition, ES/NFI and MPCA sectors. EOC DICAC, a long-standing faith-based partner in North Shewa, will manage CCCM, WASH and GBV activities, as well as strengthening networking and partnerships with local stakeholders. Meanwhile, AWA, a women-led NGO, will oversee general protection activities.nbsp ltbrgtWith a total budget of $800,000 distributed among the sectors, the project will enhance CCCM by improving coordination, information management community participation, supporting self-government improving the site area. The project will also carry out rehabilitation decommissioning activities. The ES/NFI component will provide integrated shelter emergency NFI kits, as well as ESNFI kits (in kind and cash), mobility-adapted ESNFI kits emergency shelter kits. Rental support will be provided for IDPs unable to access collective sites. The most vulnerable IDPs will receive MPCA via financial service providers. Right holders will be identified using pre-qualified criteria a verification process will be conducted to ensure that the correct beneficiaries are selected. ltbrgtThe WASH component will rehabilitate non-functional water schemes, construct latrines for IDPs, supply WASH non-food items (NFIs), empower WASH committees, distribute water treatment chemicals and promote sanitation and hygiene. In the health sector, initiatives will include producing IEC/BCC materials, deploying a mobile health team with essential medical supplies and prepositioning medical supplies. Healthcare providers will receive IMNCI training. Treatment for injuries individuals with disabilities will be prioritised, alongside training health workers in the minimum initial service package (MISP) conducting monthly psychosocial awareness meetings for IDPs.ltbrgtThe Nutrition sector will address acute malnutrition by supporting SC and OTP centres, delivering infant and young child feeding (IYCF) training and conducting routine screenings for acute malnutrition. Training on IYCF-E will also be provided to healthcare providers mobile health teams.ltbrgtGeneral protection support includes protection monitoring, cash interventions to minimise exposure to protection risks negative coping mechanisms, and vulnerability screening. The GBV component includes comprehensive case management, MHPSS, cash assistance dignity kits, as well as community-based prevention.ltbrgtBy integrating emergency assistance with early recovery elements and involving local entities such as Health Extension Workers (HEW) and community organisations (e.g. M2M and F2F networks), the initiative aims to restore vital services, safeguard lives and promote recovery, in line with Strategic Objectives 2 and 3 of the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan. Local execution through DICAC and AWA will ensure the project's contextual relevance and sustainability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
